With AI perception technology rapidly advancing into outdoor applications, robotic lawn mowers are undergoing a critical transition from automated execution to autonomous decision-making. In the field of smart garden robotics, MOVA has pioneered the AI binocular vision robotic lawn mower ViAX series and achieved deep integration of 3D high-precision LiDAR with AI vision in its latest LiDAX Ultra AWD series. By introducing core perception technologies from the autonomous driving sector into garden scenarios, MOVA has developed a multi-sensor fusion system centered on AI vision, endowing robotic mowers with near-autonomous-driving-level environmental understanding and decision-making capabilities, marking the official entry of lawn mowers into the "era of autonomous decision-making."

World's First Binocular Vision AI Perception: Enabling Robotic Lawn Mowers to "Understand" the World  
MOVA has successfully adapted multi-sensor fusion technology and AI vision algorithms from autonomous driving to robotic lawn mowers. Equipped with dual 1080P HDR ultra-high-definition color cameras and its proprietary UltraEyes™ 1.0 AI binocular vision fusion system, the mowers utilize deep learning algorithms for real-time semantic segmentation and object recognition of captured images. The system accurately distinguishes between lawn and non-lawn areas, such as flower beds, pathways, and sandy patches, and can identify over 300 common garden obstacles, including pets, children, hoses, toys, and hedgehogs, ensuring operational safety at its core.

En el campo de los robots inteligentes para jardines, MOVA ha sido pionera en lanzar la serie ViAX de robots cortacésped con visión binocular de IA, y en su última serie LiDAX Ultra AWD ha logrado una integración profunda del lidar 3D de alta precisión con la visión de IA. On March 27, 2026, at the Shanghai Xuhui West Bund International Conference Center, a dialogue on the deep integration of talent and industry in the AI era unfolded. As one of the key forums of the 2026 Global Developer Pioneer Summit (GDPS2026), the Science and Technology Innovation Partner Ecosystem Conference, themed "Symbiosis in Innovation, Uniting for the New," gathered heavyweight guests from academia and industry. These included Huang Qifan, Executive Vice Chairman of the Academic Committee of the China Institute for Innovation and Development Strategy and former Mayor of Chongqing; Liu Shaoxuan, Vice Dean of the Antai College of Economics and Management at Shanghai Jiao Tong University and Executive Dean of the Bank of China Technology and Finance Institute; and Ge Dongdong, Dean of the Institute of Intelligent Computing at Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Co-founder and Chief Scientist of Shanshu Technology. Together, they explored a defining question of the era: as artificial intelligence transitions from technological breakthroughs to practical applications, how can we cultivate science and technology innovation partners and promote the integration of industry and research?

During the global innovation transformation project roadshow session of the conference, judges from the Zhejiang Entrepreneurs Association, TusStar, Yuanfen Investment, and Yunfeng Capital provided professional evaluations, in-depth communication, and on-site guidance for various enterprise projects. They helped companies clarify development strategies, address implementation challenges, and define pathways for advancement.

The defining question of the era: Industry calls for a science and technology innovation partner ecosystem to overcome challenges in technology, business, and industry collaboration.

Currently, artificial intelligence is rapidly empowering countless industries. From cutting-edge explorations in scientific AI to deep integration into industrial scenarios, the high-quality development of the AI industry urgently requires a seamless collaborative system across technology, business, and industry. However, the sector still faces deep-seated bottlenecks: a disconnect between research outcomes and market demand, and misalignment between technology and capital.
